findings.finding: Round 1: signal promoted markdown-only and TypeScript plugins from generic to the Python profile. Fixed and closed in round 2 (Python-only gate).

folder_structure is the generic profile's monorepo layout; follow-up to describe a customer plugin layout. Accepted (spec asks for the same layout).

The `claude-plugin` runtime key is a matching signal, not a version, but it is written into the same `stack.runtime` dict whose values every other consumer treats as "<tool> version: <version>". `_extract_constraints` special-cases it, but any other reader of `stack.runtime` in the snapshot (brief generators, docs writers, downstream tooling) will render it as e.g. "Claude-plugin version: .claude-plugin/". Only one consumer is patched.
findings.suggestion: Either namespace the signal outside `runtime` (e.g. `stack.plugin_signal`), or grep the codebase for other `stack["runtime"]` consumers and skip the key there too. Also bump `SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` since the runtime shape changed.

findings.finding: test_bundled_claude_plugin_profile_can_be_selected_by_name` only calls `check_profile`, which validates the name against the resolver — the test's own docstring concedes "nothing is special-cased". It would pass for any existing profile name and doesn't demonstrate that `/shipwright-project` (the interview listing) actually surfaces `claude-plugin` to the user.
findings.suggestion: Add an assertion against the profile-listing path the skill uses (e.g. that `claude-plugin` appears in the offered names), so a regression in listing wouldn't slip through.

findings.finding: stack.setdefault("signals", []).append(SIGNAL)` appends without deduplication; if `analyze` were ever re-run on an already-annotated stack (or the signal logic is reused on a cached snapshot), the signal appears twice. Harmless today because `analyze` runs it once, but fragile.
findings.suggestion: Guard with `if SIGNAL not in stack["signals"]` before appending.

findings.finding: assert result["confidence"] >= 0.30` pins an arbitrary internal threshold; the AC only requires the generic profile still matches. If the matcher's confidence scale changes, this test breaks for a non-defect.
findings.suggestion: Drop the numeric threshold and assert only the match and score ordering (which is the actual AC). Docs and CI/CodeQL wiring are updated consistently.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes; the work is sound and well-tested, but the `claude-plugin` key leaking into `stack.runtime` for unpatched consumers is worth cleaning up before merge.
